formal_statement_detection.alias_rule: An additional formal-prefix label before the first governed prose token of an already detected heading is an alias on that statement, not a new statement. Every other inline formal-prefix label creates one inline labeled formal-statement node.
formal_statement_detection.kind_rule: For heading nodes, derive statement_kind from the literal heading macro, never from the label prefix. For standalone inline formal labels without a heading macro, use statement_kind INLINE_LABELED_CLAIM and preserve the prefix only as a locator attribute.
formal_statement_detection.macro_definition_rule: Do not count heading command names occurring as the command argument of newcommand, renewcommand, providecommand, or DeclareRobustCommand; only actual balanced two-argument invocations in document content create nodes.
formal_statement_detection.statement_boundary_rule: A heading statement runs from the balanced-brace heading invocation through the last semantic paragraph before the first explicit Proof/Derivation marker, next formal heading, or section boundary. A balanced-brace TeX lexer is required; regex-only parsing is forbidden for titles containing nested braces.
formal_statement_detection.status_link_rule: Record every status node inside the statement boundary in source order. Derive its machine role from the literal value: HYPOTHESIS premise, DEFINITION declaration, ESTABLISHED conclusion, CONJECTURE conjecture, NUMERICAL numerical_observation, OPEN open_obligation, NOT-CLAIMED boundary. Do not discard an early premise status merely because a later conclusion status exists, and do not require exactly one status per formal statement.

status_node_detection.token: literal invocation of status with one of the seven allowed values
status_node_detection.governed_span: From the end of the preceding status token or structural boundary to the end of this status token, trimmed to the nearest blank-line-delimited semantic paragraph while retaining intervening displays; exact raw byte offsets win over heuristic prose boundaries.
status_node_detection.nearest_anchor_rule: Record the nearest enclosing formal label; otherwise the nearest preceding structural label in the same section; otherwise file::<canonical-path>::<full digest of normalized paragraph opening>. The literal label is authoritative even when its prefix disagrees with the heading kind.
status_node_detection.normalization_rule: For semantic-key hashing only: with a TeX-aware lexer that honors escaped percent signs, verb commands, and verbatim-like environments, remove comments; delete exactly the current status token; normalize CRLF and CR to LF; then collapse Unicode whitespace to one ASCII space and trim. Do not normalize TeX commands, Unicode punctuation, or mathematical semantics.
status_node_detection.byte_offset_rule: All byte_start, byte_end, and revision locators are zero-based offsets into the canonical Git-clean byte stream, decoded as strict UTF-8 only for token recognition. Character offsets are never substituted for byte offsets.
status_node_detection.taxonomy_rule: The seven status-taxonomy rows are structural exceptions keyed taxonomy::<STATUS>; they are inventoried but are not ordinary governed claim paragraphs.
status_node_detection.formal_status_rule: Do not assume the first status after a formal heading governs its conclusion. Premises can carry HYPOTHESIS before a later ESTABLISHED conclusion; preserve all ordered formal-to-status links and derive roles from the literal values.
